purpose: Reference for test authors. Record NetBox objects read or changed by each test area; this file is not loaded by pytest.
ownership: All integration tests use the main NetBox database. Each mutating test area should own distinct records and delete only those records. Branches are used only by tests that explicitly verify branch behavior. This manifest is an author reference and is not loaded by pytest.
known_overlaps: Other sync task files still use the original fn-ceos-* FakeNOS dataset. Audit their records before adding new parallel sync tests.

interfaces: ceos-spine-1:Loopback0 (virtual, description RID; read by Nornir Jinja filter tests)

test_ipam.py::TestCreateIP::test_create_.coverage: Allocates an IP in VRF1 inside a branch using a dedicated parent seeded in main before branch creation.

test_ipam.py::TestCreateIP::test_create_.coverage: Indexed and next-available allocation use an explicit VRF and ignore an existing global IP on the same interface. Repeated VRF and tag requests are unchanged. Omitting VRF reuses the global IP even though the interface belongs to VRF1.

test_ipam.py::TestCreateIP::test_ip_inde.cleanup: Fails before writes if reserved records exist. Deletes only IPs in its owned prefix and its created interface and prefix, including after partial setup.

test_ipam.py::TestCreateIP::test_ip_inde.coverage: Explicit index-1 and index-2 calls with mask_len=31 both return the existing child-subnet address 198.19.248.16/31; exactly one global IP remains; global child creation and lookup preserve an identical owned VRF1 child and parent.

test_ipam.py::TestCreateIP::test_indexed.coverage: An indexed VIP creates a separate interface assignment while retaining the original unassigned record. Compares address, role and assignment tuples to explicit values.

test_fhrp.py::TestSyncVrrp.coverage: XR getter and sync tests cover compatible per-device action previews, including group and VIP field changes, dual-stack groups, VIP creation, reuse (including an unassigned VIP for an existing group), role normalization, conflict protection during dry runs and writes, and idempotency. Priority-only updates leave group and VIP records unchanged. VIP drift keeps the existing group and assignment, creates the live VIP, and retains the old VIP unchanged. Persistent fn-vrrp-vrf-* hosts use the same VIP and group ID in BLUE, RED and global VRFs. Cover later peer discovery, named VIP VRF shortcut, creation-only vip_use_vrf, preservation of existing VIP VRFs, missing VRF reporting and ambiguous groups.
test_fhrp.py::TestSyncVrrp.persistent_seed: tests/netbox_data.py uses the regular vrfs, devices, interfaces, prefixes, vrrp_groups and ip_addresses dictionaries. Full population creates VRFs and interfaces, then FHRP groups/assignments, then VIPs. --vrrp manages only dictionary-defined groups/assignments; --ip-addresses manages their VIPs. Test fixtures reset mutable VIPs/groups before exercising sync.
test_fhrp.py::TestSyncVrrp.cleanup: XR tests use sync_vrrp_fixture to clean class-owned VIPs and groups while retaining seeded devices and interfaces. VRF tests reset only owned VIPs/groups and preserve baseline devices, VRFs, interfaces, prefix and running hosts. The missing-VRF test restores TEST_VRRP_BLUE and owned Vlan10 references in finally. In netbox_data.py, IP cleanup deletes VIP dictionaries before VRRP cleanup deletes group dictionaries; device/interface, prefix and VRF cleanup use their existing dedicated functions. Test fixtures never stop the shared FakeNOS network.

test_fhrp.py::TestSyncVrrpAristaPeers.coverage: Includes test_sync_vrrp_joins_existing_group_in_later_call: syncs owned peers separately, verifies VIP and group reuse, preserved name, dry-run and idempotency, including joining a group whose authentication is repaired in the same call. Uses the class-owned Vlan250 and 198.18.252.1 records and existing cleanup.
